subject: MSA term-cycle, auto-renew mechanics & termination for convenience — redline coordination

Subject: RE: Draft MSA — term + auto-renew questions

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for sending the draft. Our legal/procurement team ran a quick pass and attached a redline with two items that will block approval unless we can land a compromise: 1) the termination-for-convenience language — they want it mutual and with a 60-day notice, and 2) the auto-renew mechanics — procurement needs an explicit opt-out window and clarity on when billing will renew.

Can you confirm Redwood's comfort with: mutual termination-for-convenience (60 days), and an opt-out notice window no shorter than 45 days before each renewal? If you have standard guardrails (e.g., early-offboarding support, transition assistance), include those in the reply — procurement will need that in the SOW/orderform.

I've attached "Hercules_MSA_v3_redlines.docx" with commentary. We can do a quick call if easier — procurement is in the loop (procurement@herculesanalytics.com).

Thanks,
Emma Li
Senior Procurement Manager
Hercules Analytics

Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA — term + auto-renew questions

Emma — thanks for the redline and the clear ask. Looping in Laura (Sales Ops) and Marissa (Legal) to align on a recommended compromise. Quick answers up front: we are open to mutual termination for convenience and an opt-out window, but need to balance with committed capacity and billing cutovers for Dedicated.

Suggested commercial compromise that I think will be acceptable to both sides:
- Mutual termination for convenience: 60 days' notice, but limited to outside any active committed capacity period (i.e., not during a locked 12-month prepaid block).
- Auto-renew: automatic 12-month renewal by default; customer must provide notice to opt out at least 45 days before the renewal effective date.
- If termination occurs within 60 days after a renewal that consumed committed capacity, pro-rate refunds for unused Dedicated capacity; Redwood will provide transition support for up to 30 days (basic offboarding documentation + two knowledge-transfer sessions).

Marissa / Laura — can you review the legal wording that would reflect the above and confirm if Redwood needs any additional executive approval for the capacity carveout? If you prefer, I can schedule a 30-min sync with Hercules procurement tomorrow.

Action items: I will attach a marked MSA with the above language after Marissa confirms.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Li <emma.li@herculesanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA — term + auto-renew questions

Thanks for the context. I reviewed Hercules' redlines and Karthik's proposed compromise. Below is proposed legal language and a few clarifying asks from legal: please confirm before we generate a marked PDF.

1) Term and Renewal (proposed):
"The Initial Term shall commence on the Effective Date and continue for twelve (12) months. Thereafter, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive twelve (12) month Renewal Terms unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least forty-five (45) days prior to the end of the then-current Term."

2) Termination for Convenience (proposed):
"Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to the other party; provided that such termination shall not apply to any pre-paid, non-refundable committed capacity for the then-current paid term. In the event of termination for convenience, Redwood shall provide commercially reasonable transition assistance for up to thirty (30) days and refund, on a pro-rata basis, any pre-paid amounts for capacity not delivered."

Legal clarifications / asks:
- The commercial carveout (no termination during committed capacity) needs to be called out in Order Form language as well — Laura, can you add a sentence in the order form template that ties committed capacity periods to refund mechanics?
- We prefer "commercially reasonable transition assistance" rather than a specific guarantee on number of sessions, but are OK including a short list of deliverables (handover doc + up to two sessions). Can Hercules confirm that is acceptable?
- If Hercules requires unconditional termination-for-convenience (i.e., even during committed capacity), we will need a compensation mechanism (early termination fee).

I'll drop a clean + marked MSA (MSA_v3_clean_and_marked.pdf) into the thread once we settle the bullet points. Happy to jump on a call with Hercules legal/procurement if they'd like to walk through the language.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Lead Counsel, Redwood Inference
Legal — Contracts & Commercial

Marissa / Karthik — appreciate the quick review and proposed wording. A few notes from procurement:
- The 45-day opt-out window is acceptable.
- The carveout around pre-paid committed capacity is acceptable as long as there is a clear pro-rata refund mechanism and a defined transition deliverable list (we need the two sessions + handover doc explicitly listed in the order form).
- Procurement requests a single marked PDF to circulate internally — once we have the marked MSA we can fast-track to signature and procurement will place a PO contingent on final DocuSign envelope.

Two asks before we sign: 1) can Redwood confirm whether billing will re-start at midnight UTC on the renewal effective date? We need that technicality for system cutovers, and 2) please provide the DocuSign envelope once ready so procurement can confirm signer list.

If everything is in line we'll sign next week — can Redwood commit to returning the marked PDF by close of business Monday?

Thanks,
